sentences: You’ve heard it before: the best camera is the one you have with you, and premium compact cameras are what you should be carrying.
Sometimes you want the power of a mirrorless camera or your DSLR, but they're too big to carry regularly.
You don’t need to sacrifice by leaving a camera at home.
A premium compact camera solves your problem.
For many, these cameras are usually out of budget, but as always, there is a solution.
Buying a new camera these days is a challenge in itself.
They are either out of stock or overpriced, but MPB has them.
These days, the best camera you carry is your cell phone.
For others, with a keen eye and a love of quality, the phone doesn’t cut it.
The main reasons to choose a premium compact camera are a larger sensor, real optics, and better low-light performance.
It is also about the tactile experience you're already used to.
A viewfinder, camera modes, dials, and a deliberate way of shooting.
These cameras also lead to a different way of seeing.
They let you still be a photographer when you need to be, with the quality you are used to, even when that is not your primary goal, but you still need to scratch that creative itch.
Over the last few years, I have been looking at used gear more than ever.
You can find many cameras at great value on the used market.
Many photographers trade in gear for a number of reasons: they didn’t like the camera, they use it less than before, or they just want an upgrade.
Often, used gear sits unused; you can get new-to-you gear at a great value and in great condition, often like new.
Availability is another reason to purchase used gear.
Sometimes new cameras are out of stock, and they show up on the used market, like the Fujifilm X100VI , which was available used when it wasn't available new.
Maybe you're eyeing a discontinued camera.
For the longest time, I shied away from used gear because I had trust issues.
You never really knew what you were getting because the available images didn’t match the item you’d receive.
I can now see the photos of the item I am receiving, with no surprises.
The biggest plus of used gear for me has been the trade-in.
I purchased a used Nikon D850 ; I traded in my D750 and, in the end, upgraded to a mint-condition camera for only $500!
With the holidays around the corner, used premium compact cameras let you trade up for great value.
Here are my picks for every budget.

The Leica Q2 includes a 47.3-megapixel full frame sensor, weather sealing across the entire body, a built-in Summilux 28mm f/1.7 lens, an electronic viewfinder, quick autofocus and burst mode, 4K video recording, a redesigned button layout, and a more refined design.
The Leica Q2 is for the serious photographer who wants one camera that does a lot with very little, and who appreciates the craft and the name.
This sleek premium camera combines timeless design with a robust 26.1-megapixel sensor and a crisp 23mm f/2 fixed lens.
Ideal for travel, street, and daily photography, its redesigned lens enhances edge-to-edge sharpness.
The tilting touchscreen and weather resistance (with optional filter) increase its versatility.
With Fujifilm’s well-known film simulations, it offers a tactile, creative shooting experience in a compact package.
The Fujifilm X100V is for the creative photographer who wants a camera that feels as good as the pictures look.
Top-speed AF meets superzoom range.
Now, it’s easier to capture more stunning stills and movies at every opportunity.

The RX10 IV is much more than a solid, smart all-in-one compact — it packs enough groundbreaking innovations for even professionals to marvel at, from an ultra-fast AF system to legendary optics throughout its 25x zoom range, to extraordinarily precise, powerful image processing, and more.
The Sony RX10 IV is for the photographer who wants huge reach in a single package without carrying a bag of lenses.

The "ultimate snap shooter," designed exclusively for monochrome photography, the Ricoh GR IV Monochrome is a specialized version of the popular compact fixed-lens camera, featuring a unique sensor that has been modified to solely record black-and-white imagery.

Beyond the black-and-white-only 25.7 MP sensor, this distinct Monochrome model also features a built-in, selectable red contrast filter that replaces the standard edition GR IV's ND filter, plus new monochrome-specific Image Control options and an updated exterior design with an overall monochrome aesthetic.

Beyond these updates, the camera is virtually identical to the standard edition GR IV, including the 28mm-equivalent lens, fast AF, refined Shake Reduction, and the improved wireless settings control via the GR WORLD app.
The Ricoh GR IV Monochrome is for photographers who already think in black and white and want a pocket camera built only for that.
The Sony Cyber-shot RX100 Mark VI takes 20-megapixel photos and records 4K video.
Its integrated zoom lens, offering a focal range of 24–200mm (full frame equivalent), is especially notable for a portable compact camera.
The Sony RX100 VI is for travelers who want real zoom range in a camera that genuinely fits in a pocket.
Buying a premium compact is more than just having a powerful camera in your pocket or your bag.
It's an invitation to always be creative and see things differently, even when that is not your primary goal.

Buying these cameras used offers great value in the used camera market, and buying through MPB not only gives you a fair price, but also ensures that the items that arrive at your door are what you purchased, with no surprises.
I've had my eye on a D850 too.
No real logical reason to upgrade from my D800 since it does everything I need, but you know how it is... the logical choice is not always the one we make.
I've also been watching the price at B&H where the new D850 bounces around between roughly $2500 and $2000.
I would definitely choose used instead of $2500 new, but not so sure about used at $1700 rather than new at $2000.
Waiting to see if there's a bigger sale during the holidays, and trying to convince myself that I need the camera... which I really don't.
